run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:10:14Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chaos-mesh fault injected into the ad service. frontend-proxy's own error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were near zero (~0.005–0.044 spans/s) until 09:16:14Z and then rose to 0.93–2.42 spans/s at every reading from 09:17:14Z to 09:26:14Z; the alert's annotated value 2.1111111111111107 equals the frontend-proxy reading at 09:21:14Z exactly. The errors on frontend-proxy are only the `ingress` and `router frontend egress` spans, and in frontend they are only the `grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds` client spans plus their parents `GET /api/data` and `executing api route (pages) /api/data` (identical rates), while frontend's cart and checkout routes show zero error spans. The ad service's only error spans are `oteldemo.AdService/GetAds` server spans, appearing from the 09:17:14Z reading, and its pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg logged gRPC server-stream exceptions. Chaos evidence ties this to chaos-mesh: Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return spawned JVMChaos objects every minute from 09:15:53Z to 09:24:53Z, and nine JVMChaos `Applied` events read `Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad`, the first at 09:16:03Z. All otel-demo pods, including ad, frontend and frontend-proxy, were Running and ready with 0 restarts, so this is not a crash, eviction or restart. The alert's stated start 09:10:14Z precedes the first observed error deviation (09:17:14Z) by about 7 minutes; the reason for that offset could not be verified.

claims.text: Service frontend-proxy span error rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, 2-minute rate sampled each minute) stayed between 0 and 0.044 spans/s from 09:02:14Z through 09:16:14Z, then read 0.9667 at 09:17:14Z and 0.93–2.42 spans/s at every reading from 09:18:14Z to 09:26:14Z, falling to 1.4973 at 09:27:14Z.

The frontend-proxy 10-minute-rate series shows the same step: 0.0058/0.0087/0.0088/0.0054/0.0123 spans/s at 08:55:14Z–09:15:14Z, then 0.6336 at 09:20:14Z, 1.5772 at 09:25:14Z and 1.1474 at 09:30:14Z, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans continued at 8–24 spans/s.

The alert annotation's current value 2.1111111111111107 matches the frontend-proxy error-rate reading at 09:21:14Z (2.1111111111111107) exactly in the same series; the alert's stated start 2026-11-17T09:10:14Z is about seven minutes before the first elevated error reading at 09:17:14Z.

frontend-proxy's error spans occur on only two span_names: `ingress` (0.3220 spans/s at 09:20:14Z, 0.7947 at 09:25:14Z, 0.5812 at 09:30:14Z) and `router frontend egress` (0 at all readings up to 09:15:14Z, then 0.3116, 0.7825, 0.5662); the service exposes only these two span_names in the window.

Within service frontend, error spans are confined to `grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds`, `executing api route (pages) /api/data`, `GET /api/data` and `GET`, which all read identical rates (0.6519 at 09:20:14Z, 0.9815 at 09:25:14Z, 0.3111 at 09:30:14Z); `GET /api/cart`, `POST /api/cart`, `POST /api/checkout`, `executing api route (pages) /api/cart`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout`, `tcp.connect` and the cart/checkout gRPC client spans read 0 at every reading.

Service ad's only error span series is span_name `oteldemo.AdService/GetAds`: it has no readings before 09:17:14Z and reads 0.5263 at 09:17:14Z, 0.9852 at 09:22:14Z and 0.2956 at 09:27:14Z; ad's `flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream` and `ResolveBoolean` error series stay at 0–0.0039.

In service ad, spans with no status fell from ~2.8 spans/s at 09:07:14Z to 0.14–0.44 spans/s from 09:18:14Z onward while ERROR spans rose from 0 to 0.46–1.23 spans/s, i.e. the GetAds server spans moved from unset to error status.

Pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg (container ad, namespace otel-demo) logged 453 lines matching an error pattern between 09:23:24Z and 09:25:08Z, each reading `Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@<id>`.

Nine JVMChaos events in namespace chaos-mesh carry the message `Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad` at 09:16:03Z, 09:16:57Z, 09:17:57Z, 09:18:55Z, 09:19:55Z, 09:20:57Z, 09:21:55Z, 09:22:55Z and 09:23:55Z, each followed about 50 seconds later by `Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad`.

chaos-mesh Schedule `otel-demo-ad-jvm-return` in namespace chaos-mesh recorded `Create new object: otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-<suffix>` at 09:15:53Z, 09:16:53Z, 09:17:53Z, 09:18:53Z, 09:19:53Z, 09:20:53Z, 09:21:53Z, 09:22:53Z, 09:23:53Z and 09:24:53Z (ten Spawned events), so the fault was re-applied every minute starting with otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-gbjlm.

The pod named in the JVMChaos Applied events (otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg, container ad) is the same pod whose GetAds server spans turned ERROR and whose logs show gRPC handler exceptions, and ad's ERROR series first appears in the 09:17:14Z reading — the first 2-minute window after the 09:16:03Z Applied event.

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo were phase Running with ready containers, 0 restarts and no waiting or last-terminated reason, including ad-554b849958-sk6fg, frontend-675fd7b5c5-zsgq9 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-95nq4.

Error-rate by service over the window: accounting and payment read 0 at all four 10-minute samples; fraud-detection stayed at 0–0.00179 spans/s and recommendation at 0–0.00189; frontend rose 0 → 1.2187 → 2.3004; frontend-proxy 0.0087 → 0.6336 → 1.1474; ad 0 → 0.2649 → 0.5732.

The cross-namespace event grouping over the authorized window contained no event whose involvedObject.kind is Pod in namespace otel-demo; Pod events were all in namespace data-recorders (Created 7, FailedScheduling 2, Killing 1, Scheduled 7, Started 7, Pulled 7, SuccessfulAttachVolume 7) and the otel-demo-related chaos events were on kinds JVMChaos and Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh.

frontend's cart and checkout paths were not erroring (error spans on `GET /api/cart`, `POST /api/cart`, `POST /api/checkout`, their `executing api route (pages)` spans and `grpc.oteldemo.CartService/*`/`CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` client spans all read 0), so the failure is specific to the /api/data path that calls AdService/GetAds, not a general frontend or network outage.

No pod in otel-demo shows a restart, waiting reason or last-terminated reason (all 21 pods Running/ready/0 restarts), which argues against crash, OOMKill or eviction as the mechanism behind the elevated error rate.

Hypothesis that the frontend-proxy errors were caused by pod restarts, OOMKills, evictions or scheduling shortfalls in otel-demo is rejected: all 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready with 0 restarts and no waiting/last-terminated reason, and no Pod-kind event in namespace otel-demo appeared in the cross-namespace event grouping.

Hypothesis that the data-recorders workload churn in the same window (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, Job Completed/SuccessfulCreate, PVC Provisioning/ExternalProvisioning, PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete) caused the frontend-proxy error rate is rejected: those events involve objects in another namespace with no observed identity or call-path tie to frontend-proxy, frontend or ad, whereas the frontend-proxy/ad error onset tracks the JVMChaos applications to the ad pod.

Mechanism hypothesis: the JVMChaos fault injected into the ad service's GetAds handling on pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg made that handler throw, so ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans were recorded as ERROR; frontend's `grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds` client span then errored, its `/api/data` route and `GET` spans errored at the same rate, and frontend-proxy recorded `ingress` and `router frontend egress` errors for those frontend responses. The exact injected action (a return-value fault, judging only from the experiment name suffix `jvm-return`) could not be read from the JVMChaos spec.

If this injection is not intentional test traffic, pause or delete the chaos-mesh Schedule `otel-demo-ad-jvm-return` (and its currently spawned JVMChaos object) in namespace chaos-mesh, then confirm recovery by watching ad's `oteldemo.AdService/GetAds` error rate and frontend-proxy's `ingress` error rate return to their pre-09:16Z levels. This was not executed.

If the ad fault is intentional, scope the RequestErrorRate alert or the frontend's /api/data error handling so that errors originating from the ad dependency (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and its /api/data parent spans) are attributed separately from frontend-proxy ingress errors.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule `otel-demo-ad-jvm-return` spec and the spawned JVMChaos custom resources could not be read with the permitted resource kinds, so the injected action, target method and duration are inferred from object names and event messages only; the `jvm-return` semantics are unverified.

trace-level confirmation is missing: traces_search for service frontend (09:24:00Z–09:34:07Z) and frontend-proxy (09:00:00Z–09:34:07Z) returned no traces (status no_data), so the ad→frontend→frontend-proxy edges rest on span_name/error-rate correlation, not on observed parent-child span references.

frontend pod logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-zsgq9 returned no lines for 09:16:00Z–09:34:07Z (current container read 0 bytes), so frontend's own error text and any ad-related error messages are unverified; this empty result does not prove frontend logged nothing.

kube-state-metrics queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo"} and kube_replicaset_owner{namespace="otel-demo",owner_name=~"ad|frontend|frontend-proxy"} returned no series at 09:34:00Z, so deployment availability and the ReplicaSet ownership chain for ad, frontend and frontend-proxy are unverified; pod state came from the Kubernetes pod list instead.
No error-rate series were returned for services cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping, so their error status in this window is unknown, not zero.

The rpc_grpc_status_code label returned no values and no non-zero rpc_grpc_status_code series were returned for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, so gRPC status codes behind the ad and frontend errors are unknown.

The alert's stated firing start 2026-11-17T09:10:14Z is about seven minutes earlier than the first observed error deviation (09:17:14Z) and its annotated value matches the 09:21:14Z metric sample; Alertmanager rule state and evaluation history were not available (list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no rules), so this offset is unexplained.

The data-recorders namespace changes seen in events (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, Job/PVC/PV events) were not investigated further; they are unplaced relative to this incident and are recorded as a gap, not as impact.
next_steps: Read the chaos-mesh Schedule `otel-demo-ad-jvm-return` and the spawned JVMChaos resources to confirm the injected action, target method, selector and whether the schedule is still active.
Check Alertmanager/Prometheus rule history for RequestErrorRate to explain why the alert start (09:10:14Z) precedes the metric deviation (09:17:14Z).
Review frontend and frontend-proxy application/access logs (or Envoy response-code metrics) for the 09:16Z–09:34Z window to confirm the 5xx responses returned for /api/data.
Decide whether the ad JVM fault is an intentional chaos exercise; if not, stop the Schedule and re-check ad GetAds and frontend-proxy ingress error rates.
